title: Offer editor
summary: One offer, Dice skins: what it sells defined once (an add-on, one-time, a quantity of 1), its SKU on each storefront with the store's own state and a deep link, and one base price shown as each store converts it, with territories per SKU and Steam as a copy card because Steam has no price API.
compare: Three cards in this order: What it sells, SKUs, Price and territories. The header shows the offer name with On sale as status text, where it sells and its 28-day purchases, and Stop selling… as the one page action (commerce.offer-stop-selling).

What it sells: Name ('Shown to players'), Offer id (its own field: plain mono text with a lock glyph, the SDK call as its hint, never a box), Sells (the kit's default-size segmented control A tier / An add-on, then the add-on picked from Licensing, with its kind named: non-consumable, bought once), Billing (One-time or Subscription). Quantity appears only for a consumable add-on. Save stays disabled until something changes.
An offer has no entitlements of its own: the Add-on hint says what it adds and a second line links to Licensing, where the Dice skins add-on is defined; an undeclared key can't be chosen.

SKUs: one row per set-up storefront with the store mark, the product id in mono, its type and the store's own state in the store's words (Ready for Sale, Active), and a deep link to App Store Connect, Play Console or Steamworks. No bundle id, package name or app id field exists: identity comes from the assigned app.
itch.io's row explains why it has no SKU (it sells the game only) rather than offering an action that can't work.

Price and territories: the base price is read-only text, a large tabular '$2.99 USD', with Change price… beside it opening the typed confirmation (commerce.offer-price). The hint names who changed it last and when, and that a change types Diceroll, the app's name in App Store Connect.

The table shows how each store converts it with real examples (Apple's price points, Google Play's conversion) and territories per SKU (174 of 175, Not China mainland). The last column has one action style: 'Edit territories →' for App Store and Google Play (an in-console territory drawer whose save is the L3 availability change) and 'Open in Steamworks ↗' for Steam. Steam is a copy card with the value, never an editable price.
The territory exclusion is explained in one neutral callout with its reason (no game license in China mainland).

Phone: the two-column form stacks, each SKU's deep link drops under its text, and the price table becomes one stacked block per store (name, converted by, examples, then territories with its link); Steam's copy card spans the width. Nothing scrolls sideways.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): One offer, many SKUs
Preserved (guide Ed. 04): Typed confirmations on destructive or financial actions
B17: Sells and Add-on carry license (they pick what the license gets); the rest of the offer is commerce.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: read-only values are plain text, the phone price table is stacked blocks, Stop selling has its confirmation, and the territory actions and Quantity are cleaned up.

findings.issue: [visual / affordance] In light, the read-only Offer id and Base price render as white boxed fields that look more editable than the real inputs.
findings.resolution: Offer id is plain mono text with a lock glyph; the base price is a large tabular '$2.99 USD' beside Change price…. No read-only box remains on this screen. The kit's .input.readonly is unchanged because other areas use it; flagged to the lead as a kit follow-up.

findings.issue: [phone] The Price and territories table scrolls sideways; examples, territories, Edit and the Steam copy card are off-screen.
findings.resolution: Below 640px each store is a stacked block: name, converted by, the example prices, then territories with its link; Steam's copy card spans the width. Compare item 9 updated.

findings.issue: [flow / missing state] Stop selling has no confirmation and doesn't say what it does per store; Steam DLC can't be stopped through an API.
findings.resolution: Added commerce.offer-stop-selling: L3 per ADMIN.md (an In-App Purchase's availability) typing Diceroll as a neutral word, intent caution; one line per store (App Store removed from sale now, Google Play deactivated now, Steam stays on sale with DLC 2817450 and Open in Steamworks); 'Players who own Dice skins keep it'; the button says 'Stop selling on 2 stores'. The page action reads 'Stop selling…'.

findings.issue: [visual / flow] Territories mixes a ghost Edit with a green Open link and Edit's destination is undefined; Quantity 1 shows for a non-consumable; the segmented control is 12px beside 14px inputs.
findings.resolution: The last column uses one link style: 'Edit territories →' for App Store and Google Play (an in-console territory drawer, named in compare) and 'Open in Steamworks ↗'. Quantity is removed for this non-consumable; the Sells hint names the kind and Billing says a consumable also sets how many. The segmented control is default size. The Steam copy card also lost the shell '$' prompt.

findings.issue: SKUs card leaves ~700px blank at 1440; read-only id where an input would be; name appears four times; Save nearly invisible; date line small.
findings.resolution: Two columns (form plus a 360px SKU rail) from 1200px; Offer id is meta under Name with the SDK hint; the select is labelled Add-on; Name helper is 'Shown to players'; 'Changed Sep 18 by Ada Lindqvist' is 13px on its own line; disabled Save is an outline; the price table becomes card rows beside the rail.

findings.issue: [phone] Stop selling is a bordered button at the top.
findings.resolution: Stop selling is a danger text link at the page's end; Change price is an icon button beside the price card title.

findings.issue: [wide 1920] Console pages stretch tables and attention rows across the whole width.
findings.resolution: Page content is capped at 1280px, left-aligned, from 1600px (.cm2 page cap); attention text is capped at 72ch with its action beside it.
